result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say clearly that enforcing harder should not come first, treat the copies as a sign of unmet needs, and handle the forks constructively (fold them back or adopt them as variants). B is stronger on request handling: it publishes the triage results, sets both a reply SLA and a decision SLA, and suggests trackable metrics. A is somewhat better at saying what it cannot know (whether a team lead chose to opt out), names something to stop doing (enforcing visual sameness everywhere), and suggests asking for more staff. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers reject enforcement as the first move and treat the forks as useful information. Both also propose triage, a response time and a cheaper way to contribute. B is a better fit for a two-person team: it admits the 40 items can't all be cleared, says not to enforce visual sameness everywhere, and suggests asking leadership for staff. It also gives fuller options for the existing forks: migrate back, adopt as a variant, or keep as an exception with an owner. Neither answer clearly says what to stop doing, and both are only partly clear about what they can't tell from the description.
